decisions.reason: It is very close to the firm’s core cardboard display business and the firm’s own R&D should let it learn quickly from early market feedback and improve the offer rather than withdraw it.
A pegboard-back cardboard shelf display fits the firm’s established design and production capabilities, so absorptive capacity is high and supports retention despite a flat overall market.
This quarter-pallet cardboard shelf display lies squarely within the firm’s existing knowledge base, making it likely that management keeps it as a standard variant in the range.

An eighth-pallet cardboard display is a near-adjacent extension of the core assortment, and a large integrated producer in this niche would usually keep such a related format unless results were clearly poor.

The wooden display pallet is somewhat farther from the firm’s paper-based knowledge base than the other launches, but it still builds on the same display-solving customer relationships and can be supported by the firm’s R&D and production know-how.

A cardboard quarter-pallet display for media products remains close to the established display business, so the firm is likely to retain it and refine its market application rather than exit after a short trial.
